hypotheses.claim: A closed fan-shaped head is mounted apex-first on an elongated quadrilateral handle.

disqualifiers.description: The drawing contains anything other than exactly two closed regions.
Neither region is an elongated quadrilateral, or neither region has the boundary structure of a curved fan.
The regions overlap, share an extended boundary, remain separated, or meet away from the fan apex.
The handle projects toward the fan's curved rim rather than away from it.

hypotheses.operational_definition: Assign membership when exactly two closed regions form one assembly: an elongated quadrilateral and a fan bounded by one curved arc and two straight radial edges. They must meet only at the fan apex and a corner of the quadrilateral, with the quadrilateral extending away from the fan interior. Membership is present when the non-compensating aggregate is at least 0.5.

required_cues.description: Exactly two closed regions are present.
One region has four straight boundary edges.
The other region has two straight boundary edges and one continuous curved boundary segment.
No additional curved boundary segment is present.

hypotheses.claim: The combined outline resembles a fan-headed hand tool with a straight handle.

disqualifiers.description: No elongated handle-like part is perceptually distinct.
No flared fan-like head with a curved outer rim is perceptually distinct.
The handle enters the broad rim rather than attaching at the head's narrow apex.
Extra lobes, blades, or detached marks disrupt the single-headed tool silhouette.

hypotheses.operational_definition: Assign membership when the whole drawing reads as one simple tool-like silhouette composed of a straight narrow handle and one flared fan-shaped head, with the handle attached at the head's narrow apex and directed away from its curved rim. Membership is present when the non-compensating aggregate is at least 0.5.

required_cues.description: An elongated straight-edged part reads as a handle.
A single flared part with a curved outer rim reads as the head.
The handle joins the narrow apex of the head.
Together the parts form one coherent single-headed tool silhouette.
